description:
From: Elixir Parity. Approved by the user 2026-11-24 (page /Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-mue.63.html, all recommendations). Split from fz-j8z, which landed Kernel.binary_part/3 for bodies.

Today: a guard such as `def f(b) when binary_part(b, 1, 2) == "bc"` is not dispatch-pure. The cause is the body of :erlang.binary_part's first clause (lib/erlang.fz:188): it slices with a `case` on a bitstring pattern, and guard building has no form for `case` (src/dispatch_matrix/pattern.rs:769). Guard values are ordinary words on all three paths, and `b == "abc"` already works in guards. Out-of-range arguments already skip the clause, because clause 2 only raises.

Change: a runtime symbol fz_binary_part(process, binary, from, size), a thin wrapper over Process::slice. Clause 1's case body becomes that call, an extern "fz" returning bitstring (that lane is admitted in guards). The range normalization (from = min(start, start+length), size = abs(length)) stays in lib. Guard building also resolves :erlang-style remote calls (Callee::for_call), as Elixir allows; unfolding and the evaluators don't change.

Not in scope: the allocation-free slice-compare matrix fact, to be filed only if a measurement shows guard allocation matters.

P3: json.erl uses binary_part only in bodies. 

Receive guards are out of scope (user decision 2026-11-24). Receive codegen can't compare against a binary literal at all (fz-nml.9.5 owns that), so the receive row moved there. Guard-call fix included: Callee::for_call resolves :erlang-style remote calls in guards, as Elixir allows.
Done when: an oracle fixture (01942) covers a match, a miss, out-of-range, a negative length, a non-binary argument, direct :erlang.binary_part, case guards and bodies, matching Elixir on interp, run and build. The distiller does not rise.
title: binary_part/3 is usable in guards, as in Elixir
